sample_mapping_evidence: Original donor labels, exact RNA asset names and Ficoll low-density CD11b-selected source protocol agree. Five healthy and eight OCSCC source codes; thirteen high-density blood counterparts and eight tumors excluded from this phase and not new independent donors.

source_processing: The quality of sequencing reads was assessed using FastQC and MultiQC. Demultiplexed FASTQ files were processed with Cell Ranger (v7.1.0, 10x Genomics) using default parameters to align reads to the human reference genome GRCh38 and generate per-sample gene expression matrices of unique molecular identifier (UMI) counts. The resulting gene-barcode matrices were imported into Seurat (v4.0.1, R package) for quality control and downstream analysis. Cells were excluded if they met any of the following criteria: (1) fewer than 200 or more than 5000 detected genes, (2) greater than 20% reads mapping to mitochondrial genes, or (3) fewer than 400 or more than 20,000 detected UMIs, indicating potential low-quality cells or doublets. Remaining high-quality cells were normalized using the NormalizeData function (method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10,000). Highly variable genes (n = 2,000) were identified using the FindVariableFeatures function with the "vst" method. Data were scaled and centered with ScaleData. Dimensionality reduction was performed by principal component analysis (PCA) using the top 30 principal components. These components were used to construct a shared nearest-neighbor (SNN) graph (FindNeighbors) and define clusters (FindClusters). Cell type annotation was performed using SingleR (v1.8.1), referencing the MonacoImmuneData() datasets. Non-neutrophils were removed from downstream analysis. For visualization, the uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) algorithm was applied to project the cells into two-dimensional space.
Supplementary files format and content: Tab-separated values files and matrix files.
source_metadata.source_barcode_scope: Original raw droplet whitelist; barcode rows are not called cells. Existing minimum RNA QC applied before constructing AnnData; no new threshold or RNA count changes.

title: Healthy donor 1, peripheral blood, low density CD11b+ cells
extract_protocol_ch1: Whole peripheral blood was collected via venipuncture into EDTA vacutainers (BD) and processed immediately. Blood was diluted 1:1 in PBS and layered onto 15 mL Ficoll-Paque (Cytiva) for density gradient centrifugation (400 × g, 30 min, room temperature, no acceleration or brake). The distal fraction containing red blood cells (RBCs) and high-density neutrophils was harvested and subjected to two rounds of RBC depletion (STEMCELL) followed by one round of RBC lysis (BioLegend), according to manufacturer instructions. The intermediate buffy coat layer containing low-density mononuclear cells and neutrophils was collected and subjected to two rounds of platelet removal by dilution in PBS with 2% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and centrifugation (120 × g, 10 min, room temperature, no acceleration or brake). CD11b⁺ cells were isolated from both high-density and low-density blood fractions using positive magnetic selection. Tumor biopsies were transported from the operating room to the laboratory and processed immediately. Tissues were minced into <1 mm fragments and enzymatically and mechanically dissociated into single-cell suspensions using the Human Tumor Dissociation Kit and gentleMACS Dissociator (Miltenyi Biotec) following manufacturer protocols. CD45⁺ leukocytes were isolated from dissociated tumor suspensions using positive magnetic selection. Isolated cells were washed in PBS, filtered through 70 μm strainers, and assessed for viability and concentration using acridine orange/propidium iodide (AO/PI) staining on a Cellometer Auto 2000 (Nexcelom). Cells were adjusted to 1,000 cells/μL and loaded onto the 10x Genomics Chromium Controller with a target recovery of 8,000 cells per sample.

Cells were mixed with 5’ v2 or 3’ v3 Next GEM Kit reagents (10X Genomics) and single cells were captured along with barcoded gelbeads. Following reverse transcription, cDNA was amplified, and gene expression libraries were constructed according to the manufacturer’s recommendations. Each DNA library was loaded into a sequencing lane on a NovaSeq system (Illumina) and was sequenced with paired-end reads of 75 bp.

These components were used to construct a shared nearest-neighbor (SNN) graph (FindNeighbors) and define clusters (FindClusters). Cell type annotation was performed using SingleR (v1.8.1), referencing the MonacoImmuneData() datasets. Non-neutrophils were removed from downstream analysis.
